paper_title: Black hole superradiance of self-interacting scalar fields
suggested_experiment_name: BH superradiance spin-down (X-ray binaries), self-interacting scalar
coupling_convention: GeV/f (= 1 GeV divided by axion decay constant f), dimensionless as plotted on the y-axis; x-axis is axion mass mu in eV
notes: This is a theoretical/phenomenological paper on black hole superradiance of self-interacting scalar (axion-like) fields. It maps out the dynamics in the axion mass (mu) vs self-coupling scale (f, i.e. f_a) parameter space and discusses observational SIGNATURES (GW annihilation/transition signals, BH spin-down, axion-wind NMR detection like CASPEr-Wind, and potential axion-photon signals). It does not present a clean, extractable numerical exclusion curve for a single coupling type: the results are projected detectabilities for BH-sourced axion waves and qualitative statements about LIGO/spin-measurement exclusions (e.g. gravitational-only masses 3-7e-13 eV would yield >10 signals). The pre-analysis hint of AxionMass reflects the mu-f plane, but no tabulated (mass, coupling) exclusion points are provided. Not a standard DM-density haloscope limit. Best treated as no reliably extractable limit data. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: FIG. 10 (page 29). The exclusion region is the union of BH spin-down constraint regions (light-to-dark blue shading) for several X-ray binaries (Cyg X-1, GRS 1915+105, M33, GRO J1655-40, LMC X-1). Lower boundary is approximate: the region extends near the bottom axis (~1e-19) for central masses ~5e-13 to 3e-12 eV, with near-vertical left cutoff around mu~2.3e-13 eV and a rising right edge toward mu~1e-11 eV. Dashed green diagonal is the QCD axion line; ALP DM band is horizontal.
